headline: Ben Affleck's new Netflix thriller Animals, which he directed and stars in, is getting weak reviews from critics and audiences.
score_reason: Pool 3 lowered 1: Kotaku's headline ties the film to AI, but its text says what AI was used for is unclear.
importance_line: Film-makers, Hollywood workers and viewers get a test case for Affleck's argument that AI can be used in film without displacing people, but nobody has said what AI did in this film, so the weak reception says little about it, and the account is Kotaku's own and opinionated.
summary: Kotaku reports that Ben Affleck's Netflix thriller Animals, released this weekend, is drawing criticism for thin characters, clunky dialogue and odd-looking shots, and has weak scores from both critics and audiences on the review site Rotten Tomatoes. Affleck, who has urged AI use in Hollywood that does not displace workers, told a Bloomberg event the aim was "to do something ethical", but has not said clearly what AI was used for in the film.
notes: Read from the pre-fetched text. Release date given only as 'this weekend'. Rotten Tomatoes scores stated in words, no figures.
